zh.question: 飞机那么重，发动机的向前推力怎样与机翼、空气和重量一起，让它离开跑道？
zh.observe: 先选没有迎面气流：抬翼头也没有升力。再选适中角度，把同样的速度和角度带到跑道，推进并回退短窗口。最后在相同起点速度下把角度增大到26°，对照气流分离、较小的升力系数和较大的阻力。改变速度时先保持角度不变。换窗口和阅读方式保留条件与进度；改条件会回到起点。

academic.title: 翼面压力与整股气流，是同一过程
academic.body: 空气是有质量、可以流动的物质。机翼的形状与相对来流共同形成周围的速度和压力分布，翼面上分布的压力作用以及剪切作用合成为气动力。把这个力分解为垂直于相对运动的升力和反向于运动的阻力，便于研究飞行。在产生向上升力的常见情形，经过机翼的整股气流总体向下偏转；从动量变化看空气与机翼的作用，与从翼面压力分布求力相容，并非二选一。上表面和下表面都参与这一流动，不能把机翼解释成只用下面拍打空气。上下两路空气也没有必须在尾缘同时会合的规定；以路长差推导等时到达的速度，是错误前提。本页路线由几何曲线画出，只显示绕流、总体向下转及上方分离的定性变化。它没有解压力场、边界层或流体方程，不能从路线间距推算压力或把符号视为分子测量。

academic.title: 速度与迎角：增加有条件，失速仍有升力
academic.body: 升力关系L=½ρV²SCₗ中，V是相对空气的速度，而不是单纯对地速度。固定空气密度、翼面积和系数时，速度加倍使升力变为四倍；若同时改变迎角，系数也会变，就不能仅按速度平方比较。迎角是翼型弦线与运动相对空气的方向之间的夹角，和翼头对水平线的角度不是同一个量。本模型离地上升后，速度方向改变，迎角因此减小，翼头姿态却保持不变。超过临界迎角时，大范围流动分离使升力系数下降，阻力增加；失速并非升力绝对归零或发动机停止，可以在不同速度发生。本页把15°设为教学转折点，使用分段人为系数：−10°≤α≤15°时Cₗ=0.24+0.08α；15°<α≤26°时Cₗ=1.44−0.07(α−15)。有弯度的翼型因此在零迎角仍可能有正系数，但零相对速度时动压仍为零。这些系数不是风洞数据，真实翼型、粗糙度、结冰、襟翼和来流状态都会影响结果。

academic.title: 跑道接触、竖直合力与短时响应
academic.body: 在地面接触阶段，支持力与空气的竖直作用一起托住重量；因此飞机有一定升力时，仍可能没有离地。开始向上加速需要竖直合力向上。升空后支持力为零，升力垂直于相对速度，阻力与之反向；升力不总是竖直向上，而稳定水平飞行也不需要升力一直大于重量。本页用1000kg质量、14m²翼面积、1.225kg/m³空气密度和9.81m/s²重力加速度，固定水平速度及机翼姿态，在1.2秒内以最多1/240秒的步长推进竖直响应。水平推力自动平衡升力和阻力的水平分量，模型没有发动机功率限制。阻力系数是0.035+0.045Cₗ²+0.025max(0,α−15)，不是实机性能曲线。接触时支持力只补足向下合力；离地后的来流方向随竖直速度更新。未计算机身、尾翼、俯仰力矩、配平、襟翼、侧风、地面效应和翼尖涡，也未求解整个起飞滑跑。图形中的机身保持识别用姿态，机翼姿态和实验条件一致。真实飞机必须同时控制动力和姿态；这不是操作练习或起飞速度、距离预测。

zh.misconception: 飞机没有变轻；发动机通常主要帮它向前。上下两路空气不必同时会合，失速不是发动机停止或升力归零。迎角过大才是本页失速对照的原因，不能把每一种低速都叫失速。
zh.boundary: 这是教学用的单机翼短时模型，不对应任何实机。气流路线和分离涡是几何示意，未求解压力场或真实湍流。15°转折、升阻力系数、质量与翼面积为设定；水平速度和机翼姿态由外部保持。图中高度与移动消费模型位置，但飞机几何尺寸不按实机比例；力箭头共用固定比例且起点错开。省略发动机限制、机身尾翼受力与配平、风、襟翼、地面效应及三维翼尖涡，不能用来估计起飞性能或操作飞机。

narration.label: 很重，也没有变轻
narration.text: 飞机那么重，却能离开地面。它的重量没有忽然消失。发动机帮助飞机向前，让空气经过机翼。我们先看一片机翼的切面，找出空气和机翼一起发生的变化。
narration.cue: 先展示整机与跑道，再进入同一设置的翼型切面；保留重量的叙述。

narration.label: 没有空气经过，会怎样？
narration.text: 先让机翼和空气没有相对运动。即使抬起翼头，也没有这次飞行所需的升力。现在让空气经过。它绕过机翼上下两面，流动方向和压力一起改变。常见的升力情形里，整股空气总体向下转，空气也给机翼向上的作用。上下两路没有必须同时会合的约定。
narration.cue: 比较零相对速度与适中角度；指向上下两面，不安排等时会合的配对粒子。

narration.label: 角度不是越大越好
narration.text: 保持同样的起点速度，再把翼头抬得更多。上面的气流开始明显离开翼面，这叫流动分离。超过临界迎角会失速，升力系数变小，阻力变大；发动机不一定停，升力也不一定变成零。所以把翼头一直抬高，不是让飞机一直更容易飞的办法。
narration.cue: 用38米每秒比较12°与26°，指出棕色虚线和阻力；15°只作为本页教学转折点。

narration.label: 带着条件去跑道
narration.text: 把同一组条件带到跑道。空气的向上作用还不够时，地面会继续托住轮子。足够产生向上合力时，飞机才开始离地。上升也改变了迎面气流的方向，迎角跟着变化。真实起飞还有许多条件，这一小段只帮助我们看清关系，不是驾驶飞机的方法。
narration.cue: 推进、暂停、回退再前进；比较离地与仍接触跑道的两组条件，说明固定水平速度和短观察窗口。

en.question: How do forward engine thrust, wings, air and weight work together to let a heavy airplane leave the runway?
en.observe: Choose no relative airflow: raising the wing nose still produces no lift. Choose the moderate angle, carry the same settings to the runway, then step and seek backward through the short window. At the same initial speed, increase the angle to 26° and compare separated flow, a lower lift coefficient and greater drag. Hold angle fixed when comparing speed. Windows and reading modes preserve conditions and progress; changing conditions returns to the start.

academic.title: Surface pressure and whole-flow momentum describe the same process
academic.body: Air has mass and can flow. Wing shape and relative incoming flow together produce a surrounding velocity and pressure distribution. Distributed surface pressure and shear combine into an aerodynamic force. Resolving it into lift perpendicular to relative motion and drag opposing motion makes flight easier to analyze. In common cases with upward lift, the passing flow turns downward overall. Its momentum change and the wing-surface pressure account are compatible descriptions, not competing choices. Both surfaces contribute; the wing does not merely hit air with its underside. Air on the upper and lower routes has no obligation to meet simultaneously at the trailing edge, so inferring equal-transit velocities from different path lengths starts from a false assumption. This page draws geometric curves to illustrate routing, overall downward turning and upper-surface separation. It solves no pressure field, boundary layer or fluid equations. Curve spacing cannot be used to calculate pressure, and symbols are not measured molecules.

academic.title: Speed and angle of attack: conditional increases and remaining lift in a stall
academic.body: In L=½ρV²SCₗ, V is speed relative to air, not simply ground speed. With density, area and coefficient fixed, doubling speed quadruples lift. If angle changes too, its coefficient changes, so speed squared alone no longer determines the comparison. Angle of attack is between the wing chord and motion relative to air, distinct from the wing angle above the horizon. After model lift-off, upward velocity changes the direction of relative motion and reduces angle of attack while wing orientation stays fixed. Beyond a critical angle, extensive separation lowers lift coefficient and increases drag. Stall does not imply zero lift or engine failure, and can occur at different speeds. This page invents a 15° teaching threshold and piecewise coefficients: Cₗ=0.24+0.08α from −10° to 15°, then Cₗ=1.44−0.07(α−15) above 15° through 26°. Thus its cambered wing can have a positive coefficient at zero angle, but dynamic pressure is still zero without relative motion. The coefficients are not wind-tunnel data. Airfoil, roughness, ice, flaps and flow conditions affect real behavior.

academic.title: Runway contact, net vertical force and a short response
academic.body: During ground contact, support and vertical aerodynamic force together balance weight. Some lift can therefore exist without lift-off. An upward net vertical force is needed to begin upward acceleration. Once airborne, support is zero, lift remains perpendicular to relative motion and drag opposes it. Lift is not always vertically upward, and steady level flight does not require it always to exceed weight. This page chooses mass 1000kg, area 14m², density 1.225kg/m³ and gravity 9.81m/s². With horizontal speed and wing orientation held fixed, it integrates vertical response over 1.2 seconds using steps no larger than 1/240 second. Horizontal thrust automatically balances the horizontal lift and drag components; engine power is unlimited here. The invented drag coefficient is 0.035+0.045Cₗ²+0.025max(0,α−15), not an aircraft performance curve. Contact support only supplies a remaining upward force against a downward net load; airborne relative flow updates with vertical velocity. Body and tail forces, pitch moments, trim, flaps, crosswind, ground effect, wingtip vortices and the full takeoff roll are omitted. The body has an identifying illustrative attitude; wing orientation follows the experiment. Actual flight requires control of power and attitude. This is neither operating practice nor a takeoff speed or distance prediction.

en.misconception: The airplane does not become lighter; engines usually mainly help it move forward. Upper and lower air need not meet together. Stall means neither engine failure nor zero lift. Excessive angle of attack causes the stall comparison here; every low-speed case is not a stall.
en.boundary: A short illustrative single-wing model, not any actual airplane. Airflow routes and separated eddies are geometric illustrations without a pressure or turbulence solution. The 15° threshold, coefficients, mass and area are chosen values. Horizontal speed and wing orientation are externally held. Model positions drive visual height and travel, but aircraft geometry is not to scale. Force arrows use one fixed scale with offset origins. Engine limits, body and tail forces, trim, wind, flaps, ground effect and three-dimensional tip vortices are omitted. Do not use this to estimate takeoff performance or operate an aircraft.

narration.label: Heavy, and still heavy
narration.text: A heavy airplane can leave the ground, but its weight has not disappeared. The engine helps it move forward so air passes the wings. Look at a slice through one wing to find out what air and wing do together.
narration.cue: Begin with airplane and runway, then show the wing section under unchanged settings; retain the explanation of weight.

narration.label: What if no air passes?
narration.text: Start without motion between wing and air. Even raising the wing nose cannot produce the lift for this flight. Now let air pass. It goes above and below the wing, and flow direction and pressure change together. In common lifting flow, air turns downward overall and exerts an upward force on the wing. The two routes have no rule requiring an on-time meeting.
narration.cue: Compare zero relative speed with a moderate wing angle. Point to both surfaces; do not pair particles for equal transit.

narration.label: More angle is not always better
narration.text: Keep the same initial speed and raise the wing nose farther. Flow separates noticeably above the surface. Exceeding a critical angle of attack causes a stall: lift coefficient falls and drag grows. The engine need not stop and lift need not become zero. Raising the wing nose ever higher does not make flight ever easier.
narration.cue: Compare 12° and 26° at 38m/s. Identify brown dashed routes and drag; 15° is only this page's teaching threshold.

narration.label: Take the conditions to the runway
narration.text: Take the same conditions to the runway. If the upward aerodynamic force is too small, the ground continues to support the wheels. Only an upward net force begins upward acceleration. Ascent changes relative airflow direction and angle of attack too. Real takeoff has many other conditions; this small window helps explain relationships, not how to fly an airplane.
narration.cue: Advance, pause, seek backward and advance again. Compare lift-off and ground contact, explaining held horizontal speed and the short window.
